prior_art_found.what: ViscNet / ANN glass viscosity composition models (temperature-dependence of viscosity from composition) — static property prediction, NOT a time-evolving field forecast for a working gather
prior_art_found.verbatim: The temperature-dependence of viscosity is used to adjust process variables for glass-making, and neural network models have been developed to predict viscosity parameters like the fragility index and glass transition temperature.

prior_art_found.what: arXiv 2604.00135 'Temperature Control of Digital Glass Forming Processes' — closed-loop laser-power temperature control for a DIGITAL/additive glass forming machine (not artisan hot-glass, not a forecast/rollout)
prior_art_found.verbatim: Digital Glass Forming (DGF) is a new manufacturing process for low-batch glass fabrication, and the work zone temperature must be maintained in the glass's working range to ensure good fabrication. ... a closed loop tracking controller that adjusts the commanded laser power to regulate the measured temperature.

prior_art_found.what: FNO surrogates for temperature fields in laser/melt-pool processing (metal AM, not glass; process-parameter->field map)
prior_art_found.verbatim: A Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) based surrogate model has been developed to learn parametric solution operators for laser processes from multiphysics simulations, demonstrating the ability to map process parameters to three-dimensional temperature fields across broad process windows.

prior_art_found.what: Lampworking/glassblowing craft guides — annealing and working temps described qualitatively; NO predictive tool for when glass becomes too stiff to work
prior_art_found.verbatim: the search results don't contain information about a specific community tool designed to predict when glass becomes too stiff to work with a torch.

results.exact_unused_slice: A neural-operator (SGNO-style stable long-horizon) rollout of the time-evolving viscosity/temperature FIELD of a hand-held glass gather during artisan hot-working, forecasting the closing of the workable window in real time from eye/sparse observation. Existing glass ML is static composition->viscosity (ViscNet); existing glass-forming control (2604.00135) is closed-loop laser control of a digital/additive machine with no forward field forecast and no artisan-craft framing.
results.honest_adjacency: Closest adjacencies: (a) ViscNet/ANN glass-viscosity models (arxiv 2007.03719) — but these predict equilibrium viscosity vs temperature from composition, not a transient cooling rollout of a working gather; (b) arXiv 2604.00135 Digital Glass Forming temperature control — closed-loop, machine-based, no forecast/rollout, not artisan; (c) FNO melt-pool/temperature-field surrogates exist for metal laser processing (2602.06241) but not glass and not framed as a gaffer's workable-window forecast.
results.reasoning: Across 5 reformulations (technique x application, application+AI/ML, application+simulation/control, industrial analog 2604.00135, craft community/lampworking), no work forecasts a hot-glass gather's viscosity/temperature trajectory and workable-window closure via a neural operator. The technique x application slice is unmade. OPEN.

results.exact_unused_slice: A neural-operator forecast of the cumulative HEAT-WORK integral (time-temperature, i.e. what a pyrometric cone integrates) and the interior temperature trajectory of an individual ware, inferred from SPARSE artisan peephole/glow observations during firing. No found work outputs heat-work / cone-equivalent forecasting; the artisan glow+cone framing with sparse-input rollout is unmade.
results.honest_adjacency: Strong adjacencies on the industrial side: (a) PINN 'virtual thermal sensor' reconstructs a temperature FIELD from sparse sensors (S0017931023005380) — same sparse->field spirit, but reconstruction not forward heat-work-integral forecast, and uses thermocouples not glow/cone; (b) tunnel-kiln digital twins / CFD give real-time predictive control of industrial kilns (mdpi 19/9/2219); (c) Orton's program already maps cone bend<->T/rate/hold deterministically. None combine SGNO-style rollout + heat-work integral + sparse artisan readings, so the exact slice is unmade — but adjacency is close enough that this is NARROW not OPEN.
results.reasoning: Industrial kiln thermal modeling, virtual thermal sensing from sparse sensors, and deterministic cone<->heatwork tools all exist; ceramic ML predicts properties. The specific neural-operator forecast of the heat-work integral/interior trajectory from artisan glow+cone+peephole input was not found, but adjacent sparse-sensor field reconstruction (PINN virtual thermal sensor) and digital-twin predictive control make this NARROW.

results.exact_unused_slice: An SGNO-style stable long-horizon NEURAL-OPERATOR rollout of the coupled slag viscosity + furnace thermal FIELD evolving toward a tappable condition, specifically for CRAFT-SCALE / small-furnace tap-hole control. The industrial slice (predicting slag viscosity ahead of tap, tap-timing) is essentially CLOSED via digital twins and ANN/PINN models; what remains unmade is (i) the specific neural-operator (spectral long-horizon rollout) formulation rather than ANN regressors / CFD-based digital twins, and (ii) the craft/small-scale tap-hole-by-eye control framing.
results.honest_adjacency: Very strong, near-closing adjacency: iFactory describes digital twins that 'run continuous forward simulations predicting slag viscosity hours ahead of actual tap'; converter-steelmaking digital twin tags 'tapping at the predicted endpoint'; multiple ANN/DNN slag-viscosity models and a fractional-order PINN for furnace thermal state exist; fuzzy-NN estimates EAF tap temperature; MIRS confirms robotic tap-hole hardware. The forecasting-slag-toward-tap capability itself is industrially realized. The unmade residue is narrow: the SGNO/neural-operator method choice and craft-scale (non-industrial) application.
results.reasoning: Unlike C4/C6, the core capability (live forecast of slag viscosity + furnace thermal state toward a tappable condition) IS implemented industrially (digital-twin forward simulation 'hours ahead of tap', tap-timing optimization, PINN thermal-state prediction). That makes the general technique x application close to CLOSED. It stays NARROW (not CLOSED) only because no found work uses the specific SGNO/neural-operator spectral-rollout method or targets craft-scale tap-hole-by-eye control; the gap as literally written ('no live forecast ... toward a tappable condition') is largely contradicted by industrial digital twins, so the candidate's novelty is weakest of the three.
